predecessors.name: Kingdom of Libya
predecessors.text: all of Libya: Gaddafi 'seized control of the government and in a stroke abolished the Libyan monarchy' on 1 September 1969

successors.name: State of Libya
successors.text: all of Libya, the same outline

ledger.x: 1 September 1969: Gaddafi's coup abolishes the monarchy and proclaims the Libyan Arab Republic.
1973: Libya occupies and annexes the Aouzou Strip of northern Chad.
2 March 1977: the General People's Congress proclaims the Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya.
February 1978: Libyan-backed rebels take Faya-Largeau and the north of Chad.
16 December 1980: the Libyan-backed attack takes N'Djamena.
16 November 1981: Libyan forces leave Chad proper.
16 November 1981: the Libyan occupation of the Chadian capital ends with the withdrawal of all Libyan forces from Chad proper.
June 1983: Libya returns to northern Chad.
1986: the Jamahiriya takes its final name.
11 September 1987: an OAU-brokered ceasefire ends the Toyota War.
May 1994: Libya leaves the Aouzou Strip.
18 February 2011: the east slips from Tripoli's control.
20 October 2011: Sirte falls and the Jamahiriya ends.
23 October 2011: the National Transitional Council declares 'the liberation of Libya' and the official end of the war.
2013: Cliopatria's Libyan Arab Republic row ends and its State of Libya row begins in 2014.

wars.name: Libyan-Egyptian War
wars.outcome: Border gun battles from 21 July 1977 ended by a ceasefire on 24 July 1977 mediated by Algeria and Arafat; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: First Libyan Civil War
wars.outcome: 'Libyan opposition/NATO victory - Complete overthrow and collapse of the Gaddafi regime': Tripoli fell in August, Gaddafi was killed at Sirte on 20 October and the NTC declared the liberation of Libya on 23 October 2011.

certainty.note: Libya's modern frontier is a treaty frontier (the Aouzou Strip page mentions the 1899, 1935 and 1955 agreements); the exception is the southern frontier with Chad, where Libya occupied the Aouzou Strip from 1973 against the 1955 treaty…
The Chad frontier is fixed by the ICJ judgement of 3 February 1994 ('16 to 1' for Chad); in 2011 the line between regime and rebels was a moving front the pages do not draw.
